citations.quote:
Let $t_1<\cdots<t_K$ be the distinct observed failure times in $[0,\tau]$.
For $g\in\{0,1\}$ define the risk count and event count at $t_j$ by
$$ Y_{gj}(z):=\#\{i:z_i=g,\ U_i\ge t_j\},\qquad d_{gj}(z):=\#\{i:z_i=g,\ U_i=t_j,\ \delta_i=1\}. $$
Write $Y_j=Y_{0j}+Y_{1j}$, $d_j=d_{0j}+d_{1j}>0$, and
$O_j=d_{1j}$. Since $t_j$ is an observed failure time,
$1\le d_j\le Y_j$. The expected group-1 count under the conditional
hypergeometric model is
$$ E_j:=d_j\frac{Y_{1j}}{Y_j}. $$
Under that model the $d_j$ failing subjects are a uniform $d_j$-subset of the
$Y_j$ subjects at risk, conditional on the risk-set and event-count margins.
The corresponding conditional variance is
$$ V_j:= \begin{cases} \displaystyle\frac{Y_{1j}Y_{0j}d_j(Y_j-d_j)} {Y_j^2(Y_j-1)},&Y_j>1,\\[6pt] 0,&Y_j=1. \end{cases} $$
If the study has no observed failures, all sums below are empty and equal zero.
The conditional hypergeometric model is an explicit finite risk-set
assumption; equality of survival laws with arbitrary censoring or subject
heterogeneity does not by itself assert this conditional allocation law.
The uniform law on the finite set of $d_j$-subsets is the uniform finite
probability space of [[def-uniform-finite-probability-space]].

The inclusive assignment-tail p-value
$$ p_{\rm rand}(z):=\sum_{z'\in\mathcal Z}p(z') 1\{|U_w(z';U,\delta)|\ge |U_w(z;U,\delta)|\} $$
is superuniform under the assignment law, so it is a valid finite-sample
p-value for the record sharp null. If an auxiliary $V$ is independent of
the assignment and uniform on $[0,1]$, replacing the inclusive tail by the
strict-tail mass plus $V$ times the tied-score mass gives an exactly uniform
p-value. The result uses the actual assignment probabilities and asserts no
validity under a weak average-effect null or under an equal-hazard null alone.

Let $N\ge1$, and let $\mathcal I=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ index the fixed
experimental units at the actual treatment-assignment level. Let
$\mathcal Z$ be a nonempty finite set of allowed assignments. If treatment
is assigned to clusters, each cluster is one indexed unit; no separate
probability-sampling unit is present. The index $i$ identifies that unit,
and no visit or repeated-measurement index is modeled here.

derivations.claim: Under $e_1$, the event at time 1 contributes $1-1/3=2/3$ and the later risk sets contain no treated subject, so $U(e_1)=2/3$. Under $e_2$, time 1 contributes $-1/3$, and time 2 contributes $1-1/2=1/2$, giving $U(e_2)=1/6$. Under $e_3$, time 1 contributes $-1/3$, time 2 contributes $-1/2$, and time 3 contributes zero, giving $U(e_3)=-5/6$. These are the three distinct scores; their absolute values are $2/3,1/6,5/6$.

The inclusive absolute-tail probability at $e_1$ is $1/2+1/6=2/3$, at $e_2$ it is $1$, and at $e_3$ it is $1/6$, because the absolute scores are distinct and the assignment weights are $1/2,1/3,1/6$. Therefore the p-value takes $2/3,1,1/6$ with respective probabilities $1/2,1/3,1/6$.

Its distribution function is $0$ for $0\le u<1/6$, $1/6$ for $1/6\le u<2/3$, $2/3$ for $2/3\le u<1$, and $1$ at $u=1$. On each interval this is at most $u$, including the endpoints. Thus the exact finite assignment calculation is superuniform under the declared unequal-weight law, as in [F2].

boundaries.reason: The example has exactly three allowed assignments with positive probability.

Step 3.1 checks the p-value distribution at the exact endpoints 0, 1/6, 2/3, and 1.

current_statement:
Fix a follow-up horizon $\tau=3$ and three subjects. For every allowed
assignment $z\in\{e_1,e_2,e_3\}$, prescribe the full records
$(U_i(z),\delta_i(z))=(i,1)$ for $i=1,2,3$. Thus the subjects have
uncensored event times $1,2,3$ under every assignment, satisfying the
full-record sharp null. Exactly one subject is treated. The allowed assignments $e_1,e_2,e_3$ treat subject
1, 2, or 3, respectively, with probabilities $1/2,1/3,1/6$. Predeclare unit
weight and the two-sided absolute unweighted logrank score before observing
the assignment. Enumerate all
scores and inclusive assignment-tail p-values and verify superuniformity
under this unequal assignment law.
preservation: All original valid worksheet evidence unchanged except expanded step1.1 claim, F2 citation use and input; no actual contract or manifest application by reviewer.
